tagline: Free vector graphics editor built on SVG, for logos, illustrations and diagrams on the desktop.
description: Inkscape is a free vector graphics editor for drawing logos, icons, posters and technical diagrams. Its native format is SVG, which browsers and many other applications can open. Because shapes are stored as paths rather than pixels, output stays sharp at any print or screen size. You draw with paths, shapes and text, organise work in layers, move individual nodes, and can change the SVG markup directly. Gradients, clones, transforms and text laid along a path are built in. It opens common bitmap and print files such as PNG, JPEG, TIFF and PostScript, and saves PNG as well as several vector formats. Most of the source code is released under the GNU General Public License, version 2 or later. Inkscape is a desktop program written in C++, so there is nothing to host: you download it from inkscape.org for your operating system. Features beyond the core are delivered as extensions. It replaces the vector side of Adobe Illustrator and the logo and icon work people do in Canva. It does not manage brand templates or team libraries, and it is not a photo editor. For image retouching, pair it with a raster tool such as GIMP.
strengths: Uses standard SVG as its main format, so output opens in browsers and other tools.
Lets you edit the SVG markup by hand as well as drag nodes and combine paths.
Opens common bitmap and print files, including EPS and TIFF, to trace or place in a drawing.
Text on a path, clones and gradients are part of the documented feature set.
Extensions carry features beyond a deliberately lightweight core.
limits: Vector only: raster formats are imported, and the README lists PNG as the only raster export.
Not a photo editor; retouching needs a separate raster tool.
No template library, brand kit or real-time team editing, so it does not cover Canva's collaboration side.
Desktop application with no hosted or web edition listed by the project.
bestFor: A designer, teacher or technical writer who draws logos, icons and diagrams and wants an Illustrator replacement that saves plain SVG.
